messages.author: a59c03f035656bc1
messages.subject: Re: Error in starting a session?
parts:
Hi Alexander,

Just want to let you know I probably found where looks funny. I just track the error to where functions are kept. It seems that Primitive.INSTANCE is a uniquely shared (singleton) object. So I put a synchronization on the object whenever the code tries updating the HashMaps like "builtins" and "internals", and the error does not come any more.

Probably the fix does the trick. Hopefully it helps.

Thanks,

Max

messages.subject: Re: Error in starting a session?
parts:
On Friday, October 25, 2013 11:13:07 AM UTC-4, Alexander Bertram wrote:
Ahah!
That's right the registration table of primitives is a singleton. Can you submit a pull request? 

Many thanks,
Alex


On Fri, Oct 25, 2013 at 4:11 AM, max <hlin...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Alexander,

Just want to let you know I probably found where looks funny. I just track the error to where functions are kept. It seems that Primitive.INSTANCE is a uniquely shared (singleton) object. So I put a synchronization on the object whenever the code tries updating the HashMaps like "builtins" and "internals", and the error does not come any more.

Probably the fix does the trick. Hopefully it helps.

Thanks,

Max

On Tuesday, October 8, 2013 4:12:25 AM UTC-4, Alexander Bertram wrote:
Hi Max,
That's really strange- can you post or share privately (al...@bedatadriven.com) the code that's causing this?

Best,
Alex
